memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made shoulder-pieces for the ephod, which were attached to two of its corners, so it could be fastened. Its skilfully woven waistband was like it - of one piece with the ephod and made with gold, and with blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and with finely twisted linen, as the Lord commanded Moses." - Exod 39:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Shoulder-pieces and a waistband — the parts of the garment that took the weight and held everything in place.

Shoulders carry burdens. That is true in every language and culture. And the ephod was designed so that its weight rested there, secured by a band that was "of one piece" with the garment itself.

Isaiah uses this very image of the coming Messiah: the government will be on His shoulders (Isa 9:6). And Jesus told a parable about a shepherd who, on finding his lost sheep, joyfully puts it on his shoulders and carries it home (Luke 15:5).

That is worth pausing over if you feel you are carrying more than you can hold. The invitation is not to become stronger. It is to let the weight rest somewhere else. Cast all your anxiety on Him because He cares for you (1 Pet 5:7).

Notice the waistband was "of one piece with the ephod" — not a separate strap added afterwards. What held the garment together was part of its original design.

The same is true of the support God gives us. It is not an emergency measure improvised when we struggle. It was built in from the beginning.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What weight are you carrying on your own shoulders right now?
2. Do you find it hard to let someone else carry things for you?
3. What would it look like to genuinely hand a burden to God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I am carrying more than I can hold. Take the weight onto Your shoulders and hold me together. Amen.
